title: Collision workspace free-record linking
summary: Recover ECX member routine at VA 0x5497b0 (97 bytes): set mode 9, clear five header words and +0x263c, then prepend 128 records of stride 0x3c in descending address order to the existing doubly linked free list. Preserve incoming head/count and increment count modulo 2^32. Direct caller 0x54b115 initializes head/count separately. Original reference bytes were checked against Game.exe; GCC differential tests and MSVC2013 O2 compilation passed.
test_description: 648 fixed-address original-vs-C++ comparisons: three byte-pattern seeds, six initial heads (null, two external records, first/middle/last internal record), six initial counts including wrap boundaries, and one or two consecutive calls. Compare every byte of the full workspace, external records and guards at identical addresses; additionally assert mode, cleared fields, final head/count and normal-case forward/back links. Install test-owned FS backing and check its head after every original invocation. Oracle linked at 0x5497b0 and its entire 97-byte span verified against immutable Game.exe.
known_limits: Payload semantics, mode value meaning, and opaque workspace fields remain unresolved; field names describe observed accesses only.

Inputs require writable workspace and a null or writable record head. Invalid pointers, concurrent mutation and arbitrary overlaps with workspace control fields are outside tested valid object layouts.
Reinitializing without clearing the list can create cycles; original behavior is intentionally retained.
Exact original layout is asserted for 32-bit pointers. Native wider-pointer builds adapt pointer-bearing layout and are not binary-compatible with the original game.
Return value is unused by the observed caller; routine is modeled as void. No matching-code claim or gameplay integration is made.
